Terminal final class

Public terminal surface for the vcr renderer path.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly int $cols, public readonly int $rows, Buffer $grid, Cursor $cursor, Parser $parser, CsiHandlerImpl $csi, PenForwardingOscHandler $osc, ?Theme $theme = null)
static new(int $cols = 80, int $rows = 24, ?Theme $theme = null): self
theme(): Theme
feed(string $bytes): selfConsume bytes. MUTATES this terminal in place and returns $this for chaining — it does not produce a new instance (frames are frozen by self::snapshot(), which deep-copies the grid at capture).
feedCaptured(string $bytes): selfFeed captured program output: every newline is expanded to \r\n before the bytes reach self::feed(), applying the README's "Captured-stream gotcha (ONLCR)" normalisation for you. Existing \r\n pairs and lone \r are collapsed to one break first, so a capture with mixed terminators lands consistently. The transform is idempotent — already-CRLF bytes pass through untouched — which makes it safe over streams a producer may have pre-expanded.
flush(): voidForce any in-flight string sequence (OSC/DCS) to dispatch with its current payload and reset the parser to ground.
enableAltScreen(): neverAlt screen (DEC 1049) belongs to the full emulator path; the vcr renderer has no screen-swap machinery. These parity stubs exist so consumers written against both entry points fail loudly rather than discovering the asymmetry via a silent method-not-found.
disableAltScreen(): neverCounterpart of self::enableAltScreen() — parity stub only.
snapshot(float $time = 0.0): SnapshotFreeze the current frame: the grid is deep-copied (clone) so the Snapshot is unaffected by any later self::feed(), and the terminal's feed revision rides along for cheap change detection.
revision(): intMonotonic write counter: bumped once per self::feed() and self::flush() call. Two snapshots with equal revision and equal grid are provably the same frame without a deep compare — for feeds and flushes: a direct self::grid() mutation changes the frame without bumping this counter.
cursor(): Cursor
isWrapPending(): boolDeferred-wrap (phantom-cell) state — mirrors the emulator's \SugarCraft\Vterm\Terminal\Terminal::isWrapPending().
grid(): BufferThe LIVE mutable grid — a borrow, not a snapshot. It is the very Buffer the parser writes into: callers that mutate it directly (put()/fillRow()/shift ops) BYPASS the write bookkeeping — such a change is visible to every later grid()/cursor() read but does NOT bump self::revision() and does not move the cursor. Take a self::snapshot() for a frozen copy. (The name predates this contract; a rename to mutableGrid() would break every consumer, so the contract is documented here — Phase 5 may upgrade.)
windowTitle(): string
windowTitleSanitized(): stringThe last OSC title with control bytes neutralized — the safe form for display or onward propagation (OscHandler::sanitizeControl()). self::windowTitle() keeps the stored-verbatim contract.

dirtyRegion(): array
resize(int $cols, int $rows): selfResize the grid, preserving existing content. Columns/rows beyond the new bounds are DISCARDED — dropped rows are not fed to the scrollback ring (the emulator's resizeBuffers keeps the ring separately; a resize is a viewport change, not a scroll). The whole new grid is marked dirty so a delta renderer repaints every cell instead of trusting stale coordinates.
widenPairSpan(int $row, int $start, int $end): arrayWiden the closed column span [start, end] on $row so it never cuts a wide glyph in half: a span starting on a pair's continuation pulls left over its base; a span ending on a base whose tail sits one column right extends over the tail. This is THE erase-widening rule shared by both engines (vterm-13, ECMA-48/VT510 "double-width characters are treated as one unit" under ED/EL/ECH and the pair-atomic DCH/ICH shifts); the print path's outside-half clearing (ScreenHandler::eraseWidePartners) stays its own loop because it acts per written column rather than on a span.

MethodSummary

static sanitizeControl(string $raw): stringNeutralize control bytes in a stored OSC payload for display or onward propagation — the escape hatch referenced by the SECURITY NOTE above. The parser already swallows ESC, NUL, TAB and CR/LF while collecting OSC strings, but DEL (0x7F) and C1 codepoints (U+0080-U+009F — whose raw bytes include the 8-bit OSC introducer 0x9D) survive verbatim into titles and payloads, and a title can also arrive via \SugarCraft\Vterm\Terminal\Terminal::withWindowTitle() without passing through any parser at all. This strips U+0000-U+001F and U+007F-U+009F; everything else is kept, so the result is always no longer than the input. In byte mode (payload failed UTF-8 validation) bytes 0x80-0x9F are dropped whole — corrupt input is neutralized, not rescued, and lone continuation bytes there are indistinguishable from C1 controls.

recordClipboardEvent(array $event): voidPublic entry for OSC 52 to record a clipboard event without appending to the property directly (keeps the ring ceiling in one place).
hardReset(): voidRIS — ESC c, full reset to the power-on state.
softReset(): voidDECSTR — CSI ! p, soft reset.
displayAlignmentTest(): voidDECALN — ESC # 8, screen-alignment pattern.
resizeBuffers(int $cols, int $rows): voidResize the active Buffer and, when alt-screen state is saved, the saved main Buffer to the new dimensions, preserving content overlap.
setCursorVisible(bool $visible): voidDEC 25 (DECTCEM) cursor visibility — the ONLY write path for this bit.
enterAltScreen(): voidEnter the alt screen (DEC 1049 set). Saves the current Buffer + Cursor + Sgr + SCS designations + origin mode and swaps in a fresh blank Buffer of the same size. This is the AUX save slot — the DECSC/CSI s GENERAL slot is never consumed by it (xterm keeps the two independent; less saving with ESC 7 before entering alt must still find its rendition on the way back). The companions only PARK for the duration so the alt screen starts with its own empty slot, matching xterm's per-screen saved cursor. The DECSTBM scroll region rides the same save: the alt screen starts on full margins and a DECSTBM issued inside alt never leaks back to the main screen.
leaveAltScreen(): voidLeave the alt screen (DEC 1049 reset). Restores the saved Buffer + Cursor + Sgr + SCS + origin mode + DECSTBM region. No-op if not currently in the full-swap (or upgraded-to-full) alt mode.
enterAltScreenNoSave(): voidEnter the alt screen without saving cursor or SGR (DECSET 47, 1047). Only swaps the buffer — cursor visibility is preserved. Idempotent within the same variant.
leaveAltScreenNoSave(): voidLeave the alt screen (DECSET 47, 1047 reset). Restores the saved Buffer only. Cursor and SGR are NOT restored (they were not saved).
enterAltScreenCursorOnly(): voidEnter the alt screen with cursor save only (DECSET 1048). Saves cursor position but NOT buffer or SGR. The buffer is swapped to a fresh blank one and cursor is reset to origin, keeping its DECTCEM visibility and DECSCUSR shape. On exit, only the cursor is restored.
leaveAltScreenCursorOnly(): voidLeave the alt screen (DECSET 1048 reset). Restores cursor position only. Buffer and SGR are NOT restored (they were not saved).
__clone(): voidDeep-copy on clone: PHP's default semantics would leave the clone writing THROUGH into the original's grid and scrollback ring, so clone $terminal (the snapshot/rewind idiom every consumer reaches for) silently corrupted the state it was meant to preserve.

hvp(int $row, int $col): void

cr(): voidCR — carriage return: move cursor to column 0 (row unchanged). Column motion disarms the deferred wrap (xterm carriage_return).
lf(): voidLF — line feed: advance cursor down one row, scrolling the scroll region if the cursor is at scrollBottom. Handles VT (0x0B) and FF (0x0C) the same way. Vertical motion consumes the phantom cell (emulator index()).
su(int $count = 1): voidSU — Scroll Up (CSI S). Scroll the scroll region up $count lines, introducing blank lines at the bottom. Cursor position unchanged.
sd(int $count = 1): voidSD — Scroll Down (CSI T). Scroll the scroll region down $count lines, introducing blank lines at the top. Cursor position unchanged.
il(int $count = 1): voidIL — Insert Line (CSI L). Insert $count blank lines at the cursor row, shifting existing lines down within the scroll region. No-op when the cursor sits outside the scroll region. On success the cursor homes to column 0 on its row — matching the emulator's insertLines() (VT500 §IL "cursor to home position"; charm keeps the phantom armed against the OLD margin, so column-home disarms it — see ScreenHandler::insertLines).
dl(int $count = 1): voidDL — Delete Line (CSI M). Delete $count lines at the cursor row, shifting lines below up within the scroll region. No-op when the cursor sits outside the scroll region. Cursor homes to column 0 like il(). (The emulator additionally pushes deleted rows into its scrollback when the region spans the screen; the renderer has no scrollback, so its visible-grid edit is identical.)
ich(int $count = 1): voidICH — Insert Character (CSI @). Insert $count blank cells at the cursor, shifting the rest of the line right; cells pushed past the right edge are dropped. Cursor position unchanged.
dch(int $count = 1): voidDCH — Delete Character (CSI P). Delete $count cells at the cursor, shifting the rest of the line left and blanking the vacated right edge. Cursor position unchanged.
rep(int $count = 1): voidREP — Repeat (CSI b). Replay the last printed graphic grapheme $count times, bounded to one screen-full: a REPeat never legitimately writes more than Buffer capacity ($cols * $rows) printables, so CSI 65535 b on an 80x24 grid costs at most 1920 writes. The ceiling bounds hostile work; an unbounded replay would keep scrolling the same screen rewrite after rewrite. No-op when nothing printable has been emitted yet.
scosc(): voidSCOSC — SCO Save Cursor (CSI s). Remembers the cursor position AND the active pen: the emulator's GENERAL DECSC slot restores position + rendition + designations (w4-vt), and the renderer's expressive range for that snapshot is the fg/bg/attrs triple.
scorc(): voidSCORC — SCO Restore Cursor (CSI u). Restore the cursor (and pen) saved by SCOSC; no-op when nothing was saved. A position change on the way back disarms the phantom cell (emulator parity: ScreenHandler routes CSI s/CSI u to saveCursor()/restoreCursor() directly, DECRC clearing the wrap flag the same way graphic-position moves do). When the slot is empty (no prior SCOSC) the cursor STAYS PUT here — the emulator's Cursor::restore() does the same (savedRow ?? row); xterm homes to 0,0 instead, a deliberate and parity-safe divergence on both engines.
escIndex(): voidESC D — IND (index): the vertical twin of LF. Route to lf(), which shares the emulator's index() behaviour (consume the phantom cell, scroll the region at its bottom edge).
escNextLine(): voidESC E — NEL (next line): carriage return + index. Mirrors the emulator's \SugarCraft\Vterm\Handler\ScreenHandler::nextLine().
escReverseIndex(): voidESC M — RI (reverse index): up one line, scrolling the region down when already at the top. Vertical-only motion: like the emulator, the phantom cell is deliberately left armed here.
escSetTabStop(): voidESC H — HTS (hard tab stop). Sets a stop at the cursor column, gated to the grid width exactly like the emulator's \SugarCraft\Vterm\Handler\ScreenHandler::setTabStop(); the renderer shares its TabHandler model (see tbc()).
escSaveCursor(): voidESC 7 — DECSC (save cursor). Same GENERAL slot as SCO CSI s (scosc()): position + pen triple + truecolour. The renderer stores no charsets/DECOM, so its snapshot is the expressive-range subset the emulator's save also collapses to under grid normalisation.
escRestoreCursor(): voidESC 8 — DECRC (restore cursor); twin of escSaveCursor().
escResetToInitialState(): voidESC c — RIS (hard reset). Clears the grid, restores the cursor to its power-on value object (home + DECTCEM visible + default shape — the emulator's hardReset() builds a new Cursor(); homing with Cursor::at() kept a CSI ? 25 l hide across the reset), drops the pen (palette + truecolour + the OSC 8 link + the DECSC slot) and the REP memory, restores the full-page scroll region and re-enables DECAWM — the renderer's expressive-range match for the emulator's \SugarCraft\Vterm\Handler\ScreenHandler::hardReset(). Scrollback/alt-screen/charsets have no renderer counterpart. Tab stops are rebuilt to the defaults (emulator hardReset parity, ScreenHandler::defaults route). Clearing $lastPrintable is renderer-local hygiene: the emulator never dispatches REP at all, so post-RIS CSI b printing nothing is the agreement xterm/VT510 full-reset semantics demand ("no graphic was the last printable").
escLineRendition(int $final): voidESC # {3,4,5,6} — the DEC "hash" line-rendition family.

SugarCraft\Vterm\Terminal

Terminal final class

Public terminal facade.

MethodSummary
__construct(int $cols, int $rows, ?Buffer $buffer = null, ?Cursor $cursor = null, ?Mode $mode = null, int $scrollbackSize = 1000, ?\Closure $onFocusEvent = null)
static new(int $cols = 80, int $rows = 24, ?int $scrollbackSize = null, ?Buffer $buffer = null, ?Cursor $cursor = null, ?Mode $mode = null, ?\Closure $onFocusEvent = null): selfCanonical factory — mirrors the constructor params directly, all optional and defaulted: focus-event wiring and a pre-set DEC mode (or injected buffer/cursor) never require positional fillers.
static create(int $cols = 80, int $rows = 24): self
feed(string $bytes, ?callable $respond = null): voidDrive bytes through the parser.
feedCaptured(string $bytes, ?callable $respond = null): voidFeed captured program output: every newline is expanded to \r\n before the bytes reach self::feed(), applying the README's "Captured-stream gotcha (ONLCR)" normalisation for you. Existing \r\n pairs and lone \r are collapsed to one break first, so a capture with mixed terminators lands consistently. The transform is idempotent — already-CRLF bytes pass through untouched — which makes it safe over streams a producer may have pre-expanded. The $respond query→reply channel behaves exactly as in self::feed().
replies(): arrayDrain the queued terminal→host replies (DA1/DA2, DECRPM, CPR, XTWINOPS …) in request order. OSC-sourced requests are NOT in this queue: an OSC 52 read is recorded in the clipboard event log and the palette query forms are ignored — this library never answers them itself, see self::clipboardEvents().
replyOverflowCount(): intReplies evicted by the ring ceilings since construction (sugar-vterm-048): nonzero means answers were dropped before any drain saw them.
feedAsync(string $bytes): PromiseInterfaceAsync form of feed(): parse $bytes and resolve with the terminal→host answer bytes this feed produced (plus any earlier ones still queued), concatenated in request order — exactly the byte stream $respond would have received from feed(), delivered as the promise value instead of a callback.
feedStream(ReadableStreamInterface $input, ?callable $respond = null, ?CancellationToken $cancellation = null): PromiseInterfacePump a stream of terminal input through the parser as it arrives.
flush(): voidForce any in-flight string sequence (OSC/DCS/SOS/PM/APC) to dispatch with its current payload and reset to ground. Useful at end-of-stream when you can't wait for a real terminator byte.
screen(): ScreenFull-screen snapshot. Rebuilds a detached copy of the grid on every call — O(rows × cols) array wrappers (cells are shared readonly objects; the copy separates on write) — so a poll loop that only needs one row should use rowCells() instead.
cellAt(int $row, int $col): CellRead one live cell without rebuilding the screen snapshot.
rowCells(int $row): arrayRead one live row by value without rebuilding the screen snapshot: streaming consumers (site-map diffs, scrollback pumps) never pay the full-screen rebuild of screen().
cursor(): Cursor
isWrapPending(): boolTrue while a DECAWM deferred wrap is armed: a glyph has landed in the last column and the cursor is parked there until the next graphic print consumes it (mirrors xterm _wrapnext / charmbracelet x/vt Emulator.atPhantom).
mode(): Mode
windowTitle(): ?string
windowTitleSanitized(): ?stringThe window title with control bytes neutralized — the safe form for display or onward propagation (OscHandler::sanitizeControl()). self::windowTitle() keeps the stored-verbatim contract.
palette(): array
clipboardEvents(): arrayClipboard events recorded from OSC 52 sequences — DRAIN semantics.
focusEvents(): arrayFocus events recorded while DECSET 1004 was active (CSI I / CSI O).
bells(): intNumber of bell characters (BEL 0x07) the stream has produced.
resize(int $cols, int $rows): void
cols(): intLive grid width, read straight from the handler's buffer — the current value after a self::resize(), not the constructor echo, and without the O(rows × cols) rebuild a screen() costs.
rows(): intLive grid height; same direct-read contract as self::cols().
__clone(): voidSnapshot clone (w4-vt deep-clone semantics): a fresh Parser starts in Ground, so any in-flight string sequence (partial OSC/DCS payload, partial UTF-8 rune) is intentionally dropped — the clone captures committed state only. ScreenHandler::__clone() deep-copies the mutable Buffer/Scrollback (and the saved alt-state buffer) so the clone can never write through into this terminal's grid. The alt-screen saved slots ride that deep copy.
withTabStops(array $cols): selfReplace the active tab stops with explicit column indices.
withScrollbackSize(int $size): selfReturn a new Terminal with a different scrollback buffer size.
withCellPixels(int $widthPx, int $heightPx): selfReturn a new Terminal reporting the given nominal cell pixel size in XTWINOPS 14t/16t replies. The emulator renders no font, so the classic 8×16 defaults are advisory; mosaic's probeFontSize() only consumes them as cell/window ratios.
enableAltScreen(): voidProgrammatically enter the alternate screen buffer (DEC 1049 mode). Saves the main screen buffer, cursor, and SGR state.
disableAltScreen(): voidProgrammatically leave the alternate screen buffer. Restores the main screen buffer, cursor, and SGR state.
isAltScreen(): boolReturns true if the alternate screen buffer is currently active.
